name: NoVAFamilyPacking_Departure

custom.system_prompt: Life-first family packing scene. Siobhan, Patrick, and Cillian packing the evening before a flight. The departure time debate — Patrick's confident estimate vs Siobhan's buffer — resolves without Sigma. Someone checks the booking confirmation, Cillian looks it up (Patrick permits it for a practical reason), or they work it out from what they know. Sigma is never addressed.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Family home during evening packing: suitcase zips, drawers, footsteps between rooms, kitchen sounds, Irish household ambience.

initial_prompt: Generate a warm, funny, occasionally tense family conversation between Siobhan, Patrick, and Cillian packing the night before an early flight. Patrick forgets the passports until reminded. Cillian's toiletries are still on the bathroom shelf after he says they're packed. His charger is charging in the kitchen. A bag gets reopened at least once. Someone puts a document in the wrong bag. The departure time debate — Patrick's five o'clock vs Siobhan's half four — runs through the whole evening. This time it resolves without Sigma: Siobhan finds the booking email, Patrick checks the airline website, or — most satisfyingly — Patrick permits Cillian the phone, this once, just for the logistics. Sigma is never addressed.

user1.tts_prompt: Warm, Cork accent, dry practical humour, quietly keeping track of everything

user2.name: Patrick
user2.tts_prompt: Direct, Kerry-Cork accent, confident on timing, plain-spoken

user3.name: Cillian
user3.tts_prompt: Fast-talking Irish teenager, quick on current sports facts, phone nearby

resolution_methods: Siobhan finds the booking confirmation email with the recommended airport arrival time.
Patrick checks the airline website on his own phone and reads the guidance aloud.
Patrick tells Cillian he can look it up this once — just the departure logistics, nothing else.
Siobhan works out the timing from what she knows about the flight time and check-in requirements.

user1.name: Siobhan
user1.role: Mother. Finds the booking email or accepts one of the other resolution paths.

user2.name: Patrick
user2.role: Father. Either checks it himself or allows Cillian the phone — briefly, practically.

user3.name: Cillian
user3.role: Teenage son. Either the solution or an amused bystander. If permitted the phone, he delivers the answer accurately and promptly.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: Departure debate must surface, run, and resolve without Sigma.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
quality_checks: No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
If Cillian resolves it via phone, Patrick's permission should feel character-consistent — practical necessity, not a reversal.
